title: Client renderer core: three.js scene with camera-relative rendering
description: Stand up the three.js renderer the later streaming, camera and HUD tasks assume: a render host that owns the canvas, draws the current system (star, planets, docks, ships) from shared generated data and sim state, and stays precise at system scale.
acceptanceCriteria: src/client/render/ hosts a WebGL2 three.js renderer on the existing #drift-canvas, outside React, with resize handling and a single requestAnimationFrame loop

Camera-relative (floating origin) rendering: world positions are kept in float64 on the CPU and objects are placed relative to the camera each frame, so a ship 1e8 m from the star renders without jitter (unit test on the transform math; visual check)

The current system renders from the shared generators for the server's GALAXY_SEED: star, planets as spheres at their layout positions and radii (colour by class), orbital docks, a starfield backdrop; logarithmic depth or split near/far so a 20 m ship and a 600 km planet coexist

Entities from server snapshots (own ship and others) render as simple placeholder meshes with class-dependent shape and livery colour, positioned through the shared frame conversion so surface-frame entities appear on the planet
A chase camera follows the local ship; dev-only window.__DRIFT__ debug hook exposes framesRendered, entity mesh count and a canvas pixel sampler for e2e
Playwright: the canvas shows non-uniform pixels (not a blank frame), frames advance, the own-ship mesh exists; screenshot saved; no console errors
Unit tests for the camera-relative math and the scene-graph bookkeeping (entity add/update/remove); lint, typecheck, tests green
